messages.subject: Assigning probabilities for tip ranges
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

This might be a dumb question, but I have not found anything similar in the forum or in PhyloWiki, so here it goes. Sorry if it has been asked before!

Is it possible to provide tip ranges as probabilities, instead of fixed values? Particularly when a species occurs in e.g. area A and area B, but it is much more common in A, so perhaps one would like to assign a higher probability of the species being found in A than B.

I realize this is conceptually strange since the species IS found in both areas so the probability of it being found in the range AB is 100% which is what the program technically does. But sometimes the fact that a species is recorded from both areas, even by very few individuals in one of them, bias the estimates in some counter-intuitive ways, so perhaps assigning different probabilities to each area could fix this?

Thanks and best,
Ivan

messages.subject: +J parameter
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nick,

I'm using BioGeoBEARS to infer the biogeography of Australian termites (using a time-calibrated tree based on whole mitochondrial genomes). I have assigned 11 different eco-geographic regions within Australia and excluded all non-adjacent ranges, while allowing a maximum of three areas to be occupied. This resulted in 38 allowed ranges in total.
The results are fine, but I am somewhat uncertain about the +J parameter. The LnL for all models with +J is much lower compared to the models without +J (around -277 and -142, respectively). However, I cannot imagine that jump dispersal does play such a crucial role in the distribution given the negligible flight dispersal capabilites of those creatures. Additionally, the biogeographic history is totally different between models with and without +J -- yet both histories would be possible. Could you give any advice on how to handle/interpret the results of my run?

Cheers Bastian

ps: I have attached the PDF output of my run.
